title: Mirwaiz Returns to Jama Masjid After Two Weeks of House Detention, Backs 10 PM Wazwan Deadline
excerpt: In his first Friday sermon since the restrictions began, Mirwaiz Umar Farooq criticised curbs on his religious work and welcomed the Kashmir Waza Association's move to end wedding dinners by 10 p.m.
body:
• Kashmir's chief cleric Mirwaiz Umar Farooq returned to Srinagar's Jama Masjid on Friday and addressed the congregation after nearly two weeks of house detention, according to Kashmir outlets reporting his statement.
  • The Mirwaiz said the restrictions forced the Muttahida Majlis-e-Ulama (MMU) to postpone its first district-level meeting, scheduled for November 4 in Bandipora.
  • He welcomed the Kashmir Waza Association's decision to conclude late-night Wazwan wedding dinners by 10 p.m., calling it a step toward discipline and simplicity.
  • No official statement on the lifting of the restrictions was available in the reports.

Mirwaiz Umar Farooq, Kashmir's chief cleric, returned to the historic Jama Masjid in Srinagar on Friday and addressed the Friday congregation after nearly two weeks of house detention, according to reports by Only Kashmir and the Kashmir Independent Media Service (KIMS). The sermon was his first at the mosque since the restrictions began.

Addressing the faithful, the Mirwaiz expressed concern over repeated restrictions on his religious and public activities. Such restrictions, he said, hurt people, cause inconvenience and amount to unwarranted interference in discharging his religious obligations. He said the pulpit of Jama Masjid has always stood for upholding faith and speaking the truth while reflecting people's concerns and rights — a responsibility he said he cannot abandon.

MMU meeting postponed

The Mirwaiz regretted that the restrictions forced the Muttahida Majlis-e-Ulama (MMU) to postpone its first district-level Ulema meeting, which was scheduled for November 4 in Bandipora. Religious scholars were to deliberate there on the MMU's September initiative on social and religious challenges, including drug abuse, social evils, youth suicide and environmental concerns. Such collective initiatives for social reform should be encouraged rather than obstructed, he said.

According to Only Kashmir, the period of restrictions began after his address at Jama Masjid on October 30, when he referred to the International Crisis Group's report on Jammu and Kashmir. He missed two Friday sermons in that period, and the Anjuman Auqaf Jama Masjid demanded his release, saying visitors were also not being allowed to meet him. No official statement on the lifting of the restrictions was available in the information provided to the outlets.

Backing the wazas' 10 p.m. deadline

The second half of the sermon turned to weddings. The Mirwaiz welcomed the Kashmir Waza Association's recent decision to regulate wedding feast timings — in particular its decision to conclude late-night Wazwan dinners by 10 p.m. Wazas are Kashmir's traditional wedding chefs, and the Wazwan is the multi-course feast at the centre of Kashmiri celebrations.

He called the deadline a positive step toward discipline and simplicity in marriage celebrations, while respecting the dignity and hard work of the Waza community, and assured the association of the MMU's full support for such efforts.

"Much more needs to be done about growing extravagance, unnecessary additions to wedding customs, excessive expenditure and competitive displays of wealth that have placed heavy financial and social burdens on families."

— Mirwaiz Umar Farooq, as reported by Only Kashmir and KIMS

He urged people to preserve the beauty of Kashmiri traditions while doing away with wasteful practices, making marriages simpler, dignified and affordable in accordance with Islamic teachings. The sermon combined concern over his own restrictions with the social-reform appeal that has been central to the MMU's recent work.
